selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: cron config/service state before any changes
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed Ubuntu 16.04 with vixie-cron installed, no existing cron.allow/cron.deny, cron.service active, and no opsadmin user present initially
useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin succeeded, id shows uid=1001(opsadmin)

selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin allowed to schedule cron jobs (config applied)
selected_evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/cron.allow with 'root' and 'opsadmin', confirmed file contents and no cron.deny present

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof that non-listed users are denied and listed users are permitted
selected_evidence.summary: antrieb user explicitly denied ('not allowed to use this program (crontab)'); opsadmin and root allowed (crontab -l returns 'no crontab for X' not a permission error); opsadmin successfully installed and removed a live crontab entry

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity, cron service, config)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2dffe735-a982-49f0-aa0a-19552507ae73, cron.service active, and /etc/cron.allow contents prior to restart
Backgrounded 'sudo shutdown -r now' returned 'reboot acknowledged' immediately

selected_evidence.requirement: Node became unreachable then came back; changed boot identity proves real restart
selected_evidence.summary: Connection refused immediately after reboot command, then exec succeeded again with new boot_id 66a01adf-057d-405c-a6b6-0d81c8e403ce (differs from pre-restart 2dffe735...)

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service and access-control enforcement
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot: cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, antrieb still denied crontab access, opsadmin still permitted
